answers.children: Norwegian Lundehunds can be good with children when the children are older and respectful. Their small 13-15 lb build and independent nature from puffin-hunting days on Norwegian cliffs mean they tolerate rough play only to a point, yet their alert curiosity and flexible agility often lead to playful interaction with gentle older kids who respect their space.
answers.other-pets: Norwegian Lundehunds get along moderately with other pets. Their curious and independent temperament shaped by solitary cliff work can produce some same-sex tension or selective sociability, while their small size and low prey drive from puffin retrieval allow coexistence with cats or smaller animals if introduced carefully.
answers.exercise: Norwegian Lundehunds need at least one hour of active exercise daily. Without it their high energy from cliff-scaling puffin hunts leads to boredom and destruction such as chewing baseboards, so long hikes on uneven terrain, obstacle courses or puzzle toys that mimic their agile Norwegian island work suit them best.
answers.shedding: Yes — Norwegian Lundehunds shed moderately year-round with possible seasonal increases. Their medium double coat traps loose hair that spreads through the house, and the flexible anatomy from their puffin-hunting past does not change the grooming demands of the double layers.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Norwegian Lundehund is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. The medium double coat produces dander and sheds moderately, so the alert curious breed still releases allergens despite its rare status and unique extra-toed feet developed for Norwegian cliffs.
answers.training: Norwegian Lundehunds are not the easiest to train. Their independent streak from centuries of working alone on Vaeroy and Rost cliffs to hunt puffins makes them think for themselves rather than await direction, though their intelligence of 7 supports problem-solving once an owner works with the quirky personality and moderate trainability of 5.
answers.lifespan: Norwegian Lundehunds live 12-15 years. Their small 12-15 in height and 13-15 lb weight contribute to this range, yet the dangerously small gene pool from near-extinction and dedicated 1960s recovery efforts by breeders such as Eleanor Christie ties to their low health robustness of 3 and serious digestive issues that can affect longevity.
answers.size: Norwegian Lundehunds reach 13-15 lb and stand 12-15 in tall. Their compact build packs remarkable flexibility from puffin-hunting ancestry, allowing them to contort through narrow crevices or turn their heads 180 degrees, which makes living with them feel like sharing space with a small but endlessly acrobatic explorer.
answers.barking: Norwegian Lundehunds bark moderately. Their alert temperament leads to sharp barks at unusual noises or intruders, a holdover from guarding their puffin catches on remote Norwegian islands, yet they remain relatively quiet indoors unless something specific triggers their curious independent mind.
answers.apartment: Norwegian Lundehunds can live in an apartment. Their small size helps them settle indoors, yet their energy of 7 and need for mental challenges from cliff navigation mean daily exercise and puzzle toys are essential to prevent boredom-driven destruction despite the limited floor space.
answers.first-time: Norwegian Lundehunds are not a good first dog. Their independent curious nature combined with serious digestive health issues, a tiny gene pool and specific exercise demands from their puffin-hunting history on steep Norwegian cliffs create a steep learning curve that challenges novices.
